A drive maker's own shipping back-of-house, off its loading dock: a steel cash box stands open on a packing bench stage-right, packed tight with banded banknotes, and a pallet of finished drive units waits beside it with its dust sheet folded back. On the far side of the racks a crew of packers in overalls works the shelves, banding notes into bundles and stacking them into a strongbox on a trestle. The dock's roll-up door stands open stage-left on a waiting truck, throwing a hard slab of daylight across the concrete. Framing: wide static, the money low in frame and the lit dock door high. Palette: cool grey concrete, warm doorway amber, green banknote banding.

A gold-rush supply stall on a muddy riverbank in flat morning light: a plank counter under a canvas awning, the rack behind it hung with pick heads, shovel blades and coils of rope. Behind the counter a crew of aproned sellers works the stall, passing tools across it and hauling more from a stack of crates at their backs; the board above the awning is broad, plain and unlettered. Prospectors work the shallows on the far side of the creek, bent over pans in a long line. Framing: wide, the stall foreground-right, the diggings receding stage-left. Palette: mud brown, canvas cream, steel grey. On the counter among the pick heads and blades stands one beige drive unit, out of place and unremarked.
